record.paper_title: Trimer Covers in the Triangular Grid: Twenty Mostly Open Problems
record.original_question: Let T103(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel in which right stones are allowed, left stones are forbidden, and all three bone orientations are allowed. Whenever the Conway-Lagarias invariant of the (a,b)-benzel is positive or zero, must a type-103 tiling exist?

evidence.quote: For 0 <= i, j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3 we define Tijk (a, b) as the number of ways to tile the (a, b)-benzel if the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone iff i = 1, contains the left stone iff j = 1, and contains k of the bones. We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.

When the Conway-Lagarias invariant of a benzel is strictly negative, the benzel cannot be tiled by bones and right-pointing stones; the corresponding entries in the table must be zero. On the other hand, when a and b are such that the Conway-Lagarias invariant is positive or zero, the entries in the table are observed to be positive, though I see no reason for concluding that they are.
Problem 7: Is it true that when the Conway-Lagarias invariant associated with the (a, b)-benzel is positive or zero, tilings of type 103 exist?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the triangular lattice. A "stone" is a trimer consisting of three unit triangles meeting at a common vertex; there are two chiralities, called the right stone and the left stone. A "bone" is a trimer consisting of three unit triangles in a row; bones come in three rotational orientations. For positive integers a, b, the (a,b)-benzel is a certain hexagonally symmetric region of the triangular lattice (a hexagonal region with corners trimmed so as to be tileable by trimers, as introduced in the study of Propp's benzels).

For indices i, j ∈ {0,1} and k ∈ {0,1,2,3}, let T_{ijk}(a,b) denote the number of tilings of the (a,b)-benzel using the prototile set that includes the right stone iff i=1, includes the left stone iff j=1, and includes exactly k of the three bone orientations (chosen in the standard rotation-symmetric way when k<3, otherwise all three). 

The Conway–Lagarias invariant CL(a,b) of the (a,b)-benzel is defined (following Conway–Lagarias) by: for any tiling of a simply-connected region of the triangular lattice by stones and bones, the total area of right stones minus the total area of left stones depends only on the region; this common value is CL(a,b).

Question: Is it true that whenever CL(a,b) ≥ 0, we have T_{103}(a,b) > 0? Equivalently, whenever the Conway–Lagarias invariant of the (a,b)-benzel is nonnegative, must there exist a tiling of the (a,b)-benzel using only right stones and bones (in any of the three orientations), with left stones forbidden?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is one of the "twenty mostly open problems" posed by Propp on trimer covers in the triangular grid. Subsequent work on benzel tilings (e.g., Kim–Propp's pentagonal number theorem, generalized compression methods, abacus bijection, and Lai's hexagons-with-holes correspondence) has produced enumerative results for various T_{ijk}, but I found no source claiming a proof of the existence assertion T_{103}(a,b) > 0 whenever CL(a,b) ≥ 0. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Tilings of benzels via generalized compression
status_evidence.snippet: Studies tilings of (a,b)-benzels by stones and bones, building on Propp's framework.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to investigate enumeration of benzel tilings but does not resolve the existence question for type 103.

status_evidence.title: A pentagonal number theorem for tribone tilings
status_evidence.snippet: Kim and Propp prove enumerative formulas for certain benzel tilings.
status_evidence.claim: Related enumerative theorems do not resolve the T_{103} positivity question.

status_evidence.title: Jim Propp's Benzel Tilings Site
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems and progress on benzel tilings.
status_evidence.claim: Problem listed without a known resolution.
